list.name: mode
list.label: mode
list.description: stream = one PutStream/GetStream/RemoveStream/KeySetStream (native: putAll/getAll/removeAll/keySetOnServer). unary×N = the same work one Put/Get/Remove per entry, N calls in flight. Applies to every k6 panel.

list.name: region
list.label: region
list.description: Filters the panels that read the clients' own metrics (failed calls, the gRPC row). k6 doesn't know regions.

options.content:
### 02 · Bulk streaming: native putAll/getAll/removeAll vs. GemFire for gRPC streams
One **call** moves many entries: one PutStream / GetStream / RemoveStream / KeySetStream (grpc-java, straight to `server1:50051`), or the Region bulk calls doing the same job (native-java, single-hop through the locator). `mode=unary` does the same work one Put/Get/Remove per entry, the baseline that shows what streaming buys. Load comes from k6 (`make select-load-test`); the **load run** dropdown picks the runs. *End-to-end* = the HTTP request as k6 saw it. *GemFire call* = time inside the stream / Region calls.

panels.title: At a glance: selected load runs over the time range
Peak entries/s
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. Highest entries/s k6 sustained (30-second windows) through each client, any mode.

panels.title: Bulk call p50
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. Median time inside one bulk call (all ops and modes in the selected runs), as each client reported it.

panels.title: Bulk call p99
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. 99th percentile of one bulk call.

panels.title: Failed calls
panels.description: Share of /bulk calls that failed, over the time range, from the clients' own demo_op_latency_seconds{code!="OK"}. It ignores the load run dropdown; the region dropdown applies.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(demo_op_latency_seconds_count{client="native-java", region=~"$region", code=~".+", code!="OK"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / sum(increase(demo_op_latency_seconds_count{client="native-java", region=~"$region"}[$__range]))

(sum(increase(demo_op_latency_seconds_count{client="grpc-java", region=~"$region", code=~".+", code!="OK"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / sum(increase(demo_op_latency_seconds_count{client="grpc-java", region=~"$region"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Run summary: same columns as the terminal table

panels.description: One row per client, for the selected runs over the time range (all ops and modes). CPU per 1k entries counts the client container's CPU only while it was under load.

targets.expr: (sum by (client) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode", expected_response="false"}[$__range])) or sum by (client) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (client) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode"}[$__range]))

sum by (client) (sum_over_time((sum by (client) (label_replace(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{service=~".*-client-.*"}[1m]), "client", "$1-$2", "service", "(.*)-client-(.*)")) and on (client) (sum by (client) (rate(k6_http_reqs_total{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode"}[1m])) > 0))[$__range:15s])) * 15 / sum by (client) (increase(k6_bulk_entries_total{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode"}[$__range])) * 1000

panels.title: Streaming vs one call per entry (bulk/stream-vs-unary)
Entries/s by mode
panels.description: Solid = stream (PutStream/GetStream/RemoveStream, or putAll/getAll/removeAll). Dashed = 16 unary calls in flight. Dotted = one unary call at a time. The same put → get → remove cycle every time.

panels.title: Each client against its own stream
panels.description: Peak entries/s (30-second windows) per client and mode, and how each mode compares with the same client's stream: "13× fewer" = a thirteenth of the stream's throughput. Call latencies are for one call of the cycle (2,000 entries by default).

targets.expr: max_over_time(sum by (client, mode) (rate(k6_bulk_entries_total{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode", script="bulk/stream-vs-unary"}[30s]))[$__range:10s]) / on (client) group_left () max_over_time(sum by (client) (rate(k6_bulk_entries_total{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode", script="bulk/stream-vs-unary", mode="stream"}[30s]))[$__range:10s])

panels.title: Entries/s by chunk size (bulk/batch-sweep)
panels.description: Entries per stream message (gRPC) = entries per putAll/getAll/removeAll call (native). Each chunk size runs on its own.

panels.title: Throughput by chunk size
panels.description: Peak entries/s per client and chunk size. Empty until bulk/batch-sweep has run.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (client, batch) (increase(k6_gemfire_call_duration_seconds{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode", batch!=""}[$__range])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (client, batch) (increase(k6_gemfire_call_duration_seconds{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode", batch!=""}[$__range])))

panels.title: Load test (k6): end-to-end vs. GemFire call
Entries/s
panels.description: Entries moved per second through each client (GetStream / Get: entries found).

panels.title: Bulk call p50: end-to-end vs. GemFire call
panels.description: Solid = end-to-end (k6), dashed = GemFire call (in the client). For bulk calls the two are close: HTTP overhead is tiny next to moving thousands of entries.

panels.title: Bulk call p99: end-to-end vs. GemFire call
panels.description: Solid = end-to-end (k6), dashed = GemFire call (in the client). For bulk calls the two are close: HTTP overhead is tiny next to moving thousands of entries.

panels.title: GemFire call p50 by op (op: $op)
panels.description: One bulk call per op. Unary-mode ops are named after the unary RPC (Put, Get, Remove); the call covers every entry.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (client, op) (rate(k6_gemfire_call_duration_seconds{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode", op=~"$op"}[1m])))

panels.title: GemFire call p99 by op (op: $op)
panels.description: One bulk call per op. Unary-mode ops are named after the unary RPC (Put, Get, Remove); the call covers every entry.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (client, op) (rate(k6_gemfire_call_duration_seconds{run=~"$run", mode=~"$mode", op=~"$op"}[1m])))

panels.title: Per-operation GemFire call latency (selected runs, whole time range)
panels.description: Compares p50s: "5.0× slower" = grpc-java's median call took 5 times as long as native's. GetStream is the outlier: server1 fetches every key it doesn't host from server2 one at a time (see the GemFire servers row).

panels.title: gRPC streams (interceptor): what grpc-java put on the wire
Call duration p50 by method
panels.description: demo_rpc_duration_seconds from the interceptor: a stream from start to the server's close.

panels.title: Messages/s by method
panels.description: Every message the interceptor saw. A PutStream sends one StreamConfig, then one message per chunk, and receives one. A GetStream receives entries back while it is still sending.

panels.title: Calls/s by status code
panels.description: Every gRPC call by its final status code, OK included.

panels.title: Messages per call
panels.description: Average messages per gRPC call: 1 for unary calls; for a stream, the chunk count + 1 sent.

panels.title: gRPC calls by method (whole time range)
panels.description: Every gRPC method grpc-java called, from its interceptor. The demo's calls count too; messages ignore the region dropdown.

targets.expr: sum by (method) (increase(demo_rpc_duration_seconds_count{client="grpc-java", region=~"$region", code=~".+", code!="OK"}[$__range])) or sum by (method) (increase(demo_rpc_duration_seconds_count{client="grpc-java", region=~"$region"}[$__range])) * 0

panels.title: GemFire servers: what the cluster sees
Messages to the other server
panels.description: Peer-to-peer messages a server sends to the server that owns a bucket. The gRPC client talks only to server1, so server1 forwards: a putAll/removeAll as one message per bucket, but a getAll as one GetMessage per key it doesn't host. That's why GetStream is the slowest stream. Native single-hop sends each server only its own keys, so it adds almost nothing here.

panels.title: Bulk operations per server
panels.description: CachePerfStats putalls / removeAlls count every bulk operation the server ran, the gRPC streams' too (each stream becomes putAll/removeAll operations of at most bulk-batch-size entries). CacheServerStats *Requests count only native-protocol requests on port 40404.

panels.title: Entries per region
panels.description: PartitionedRegionStats.dataStoreEntryCount, summed over both servers. Each client has its own bulk region.

panels.title: Client connections per server
panels.description: native: CacheServerStats.currentClientConnections (pooled sockets). gRPC: one multiplexed HTTP/2 connection.

panels.title: CPU: GemFire members (cores)
panels.description: server1 is the gRPC entry point: it decodes protobuf and forwards to server2.

panels.title: Client CPU per 1k entries
panels.description: Client container CPU-seconds per 1,000 entries moved (selected runs). Lower is cheaper. Empty between runs.

panels.title: Memory working set
panels.description: Watch the clients during bulk/keyset: keySetOnServer builds the whole key set in one response; KeySetStream sends it in pages.
